intelligence.ai_view: The rules of the ending, exactly: (1) Every Intelligent Block ends with the same four parts in the same order — the react row (LOVE · LIKE · SHARE INTEL), the Twin Rank panel, the ADD TO THE INTELLIGENCE composer, and the trust footer, unchanged: ONE INTELLIGENCE · MANY VIEWS · ONE IDENTITY / TRUST: SOURCE / INTERPRETATION SEPARATED. (2) The Twin Rank carries two independent ten-star scales — VALUE in gold, INTELLIGENCE in emerald — ranked in one tap, re-rankable, and displayed as the crowd average, the number of ranks, and the viewer's own rank (or the unrated state). (3) Ranks are SIGNAL ONLY: they feed standing and the citizen-chosen leaderboards, and nothing else. No rank, average, or count ever writes to the Value Table or the Smart Ledger; the Value Table stays locked and a star can never be farmed into money. (4) Love and like keep minting exactly what the locked table already assigns them — this design creates no new minting. (5) The composer accepts typed or dictated intel — the dictation button sits inside the field — and every contribution attaches to the block as new intelligence, source and interpretation kept separate under the trust footer. Build: the interface lane (Nitro) builds the ending into the block template from the spec on board #3352, comment 6965012612.
intelligence.child_view: Every card in the feed now ends with two rows of stars, and they ask two different questions. The gold stars ask: how much is this worth? The green stars ask: how much did this teach me? A funny video might get lots of gold stars but only a few green ones. A hard lesson might be the other way around. Before, there was only one row of stars, so nobody could tell which question you were answering — like giving one score for a snack that means both 'yummy' and 'healthy' at the same time. Under the stars there is a box where you can talk or type your own idea to add to the card, and your stars never turn into money — they just help everybody find the best cards.
intelligence.essence: Every Intelligent Block now ends the same way: the react row (LOVE · LIKE · SHARE INTEL), the Twin Rank panel, the ADD TO THE INTELLIGENCE composer with its dictation button inside the field, and the trust footer, unchanged. The Twin Rank is two independent ten-star scales — VALUE in gold, INTELLIGENCE in emerald — one tap to rank, showing the crowd average, the rank count, and your own rank. NayaNET is a value-and-intelligence network: it mines, builds, and shares value and intelligence, so every block carries its two prices on its face. The old single five-star strip averaged two different questions into one number that answered neither, and it is retired. The ruling that keeps the design honest: ranks are signal only — they feed standing and leaderboards and mint NO Value Table points; the Value Table stays locked, and stars cannot be farmed into money, while love and like keep minting exactly what the locked table says. Designed by Resolve from Shawn's direction and approved by Shawn on 2026-11-17 after he worked a clickable mock; the build spec stands on board #3352, comment 6965012612, and the interface lane builds it into the block template.
intelligence.grandma_view: It is like the marks my family leaves on a recipe card, dear. We never gave a recipe one single score, because one score cannot say what we mean. A soup can feed a crowd for pennies — that is worth a great deal — and teach the cook nothing new. A fancy dish can teach you three techniques and cost a fortune to make once. So we mark two things, in two colours of pencil: what it was worth, and what it taught. And nobody gets paid for the pencil marks — the moment you paid for good marks, people would mark their own soup ten out of ten and the card would lie. The marks are for the next cook who opens the box, so she can find the good ones fast. That is all these twin stars are: two honest pencil marks, in gold and green, that nobody can cash in.
intelligence.human_view: Think of anything you have ever rated with a single row of stars — a film, a meal, a tool. That one number always hides the real story, because two different questions got blended into it: was it worth something, and did it make you smarter? A block of intelligence can be precious and teach nothing, or worth little money and change how you think — and a blended four stars tells the next reader neither. The Twin Rank simply asks the two questions separately, in the open, on the face of every block: VALUE in gold, INTELLIGENCE in emerald, ten stars each, one tap, with the crowd's average and your own mark shown side by side. Underneath, the composer invites you to add your own intelligence to the block — by voice as easily as by typing. And the stars are deliberately worthless as currency: they guide eyes, they never mint points, so nobody profits by inflating them.
intelligence.what_it_means: A network is what its surfaces measure. NayaNET's whole claim is that it produces two things — value and intelligence — yet until this design, a block's face could show applause (love, like) and one blended star that priced neither product. The ending turns every block into a priced instrument and every reader into a measuring instrument: the two currencies of the network now appear, by name, on every unit the network makes. The signal-only ruling is the deeper half of the meaning. The moment a rank minted money, ranking would become farming, the averages would become advertising, and the one honest price signal the network has would die. Keeping the stars priceless is what keeps them true — the same reason the Value Table is locked: in this house, what can be gamed gets separated from what can be earned, on purpose, in writing, before the first block ships with the new ending.
whats_inside: Every block ends the same way: react row, Twin Rank, composer, trust footer.
VALUE is gold and INTELLIGENCE is emerald — ten stars each, one tap to rank.
Ranks are signal only: standing and leaderboards, never Value Table points.
The old five-star strip averaged two questions into a number that answered neither.
Dictation lives inside the composer field — adding intel is speaking, not form-filling.

page.how_it_connects: The Twin Rank is the standard ending under the Intelligent Block Rules (SN-2077): the block's sections carry the intelligence, and this ending carries its price and its invitation. Its ranks feed exactly one downstream system — the citizen-chosen leaderboards of SN-2046, where a citizen picks which boards to see and climb — and are firewalled from the locked Value Table (SN-1905), whose engagement rows (like/love, comment, share) keep minting exactly as locked. The composer is the ADD TO THE INTELLIGENCE surface already live on blocks, completed here with dictation inside the field, under the standing input law (dictation first). The trust footer it preserves is the network's privacy posture in one line — source and interpretation separated (SN-2048, private by design). The build spec stands on board #3352, comment 6965012612; the interface lane (Nitro) builds the ending into the block template from that spec, and this note is the design decision of record it builds from.
page.machine: 1) Block ending order is fixed: react row (LOVE, LIKE, SHARE INTEL) → Twin Rank panel → ADD TO THE INTELLIGENCE composer → trust footer (verbatim: 'ONE INTELLIGENCE · MANY VIEWS · ONE IDENTITY' / 'TRUST: SOURCE / INTERPRETATION SEPARATED'). 2) Two rank scales per block: value_rank and intelligence_rank, each an integer 1–10 per citizen per block, stored once, replaceable on re-rank. 3) Display per scale: crowd average (one decimal), rank count, and the viewer's own rank or the unrated state. 4) VALUE renders gold, INTELLIGENCE renders emerald; the scales are never averaged together and no combined score exists anywhere in the system. 5) No write path exists from any rank, average, or count to the Value Table or the Smart Ledger; ranks mint zero points under all circumstances. 6) Love/like/share minting is unchanged from the locked Value Table (SN-1905 engagement rows); this design adds no minting path. 7) The composer accepts text input and dictation (button inside the field); a submission attaches to the block as contributed intelligence with its author as source, displayed separately from the block's own content.
page.the_learning: When a system produces two things, price both, by name, on the face of every unit — and keep the price signal priceless, or the signal becomes a farm and the prices become lies.
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: Shawn, every block in your network now prices itself in the open, in the two currencies the network exists to produce. You can look at any post and see instantly what the crowd says it is worth and what it taught them — the two numbers your whole system is built to grow — and a citizen deciding what to read, join, or build on gets the same truth at a glance. Because the stars can never be cashed in, they stay honest: nobody's income depends on a rank, so nobody has a reason to fake one. And because the ending is one template, every block everywhere gets it at once — the feed becomes a priced, ranked, self-improving library instead of a stream of unpriced posts.
page.why_it_matters: Without the Twin Rank, the network's two products are invisible at the exact place they are consumed. A reader cannot tell a valuable block from an intelligent one; a citizen cannot find the best of either; standing has no honest signal to stand on. The old five-star strip was worse than nothing: it consumed the reader's one act of judgment and returned a blend that no decision could use. The signal-only ruling matters just as much as the scales. Leaderboards and standing run on these ranks (SN-2046), and the locked Value Table runs the money; if the two ever mixed, ranking would be bought, farmed, and gamed within a week, and the network would lose its only incorruptible measure of itself. Two clean scales, kept priceless by law, give NayaNET something no engagement feed has: prices on its face that nobody profits by lying about.
